The alphabet keeps the properties base-57 was chosen for: it folds to exactly 34 case-insensitive classes, so a 22-character field is worth 111.92 bits on a case-INSENSITIVE volume - above the 94.12 the retired base-85 grammar gave - and it still encodes 128 bits in 22 characters. Pins the arithmetic the 2026-08-27 review's T1 was answered with, so a later alphabet change cannot quietly erode it. Pester: Describe 'The alphabet keeps the properties WP12 chose it for'.

The one gap SR-061's markers leave open is proved BENIGN rather than argued: a store with every object renamed into the retired base-85 grammar, every DataPath blanked, and no witness - the worst case the gap admits - still restores byte-exact, because the locator matches CONTENT and never names. bats: tests/bash/name_grammar.bats.

Expected: canon returns non-zero and prints nothing. Reducing the .. lexically would judge this OUTSIDE the backup while the kernel resolves it INSIDE, letting a restore write into the backup root.

Expected: Returns 0, 1, 0, 1 and 2 respectively; a target that cannot be canonicalised exits 2 as a precondition and creates nothing.

Parameters: Test-ShouldPromptGraphically across NonInteractive / InputRedirected / UserInteractive / NoGui
Expected: None for NonInteractive, redirected stdin, and no-console-no-desktop; Text for NoGui; Gui otherwise. NonInteractive outranks a present desktop.

Parameters: reconstruct.sh --pick-target with FILEBACKUP_PICKER returning a folder
Expected: Restores byte-exact into the chosen folder, exit 0.

Parameters: reconstruct.sh --pick-target with a picker that cancels
Expected: Usage + exit 2; no default target is invented.

Parameters: reconstruct.sh --pick-target with no DISPLAY, no WAYLAND_DISPLAY and no picker
Expected: Usage + exit 2 rather than a hang.
Usage + exit 2, unchanged. Adding a picker must not turn the bare failure into an interactive path: a caller that forgot the flag must keep failing, not start waiting.
A single pwsh line with -ExitCode and %*, CRLF, ASCII, and NO pause - the hold is the restorer job so it cannot fire for an automated caller.

Parameters: Double-click RECONSTRUCT.cmd; then cmd /c RECONSTRUCT.cmd with no arguments from a console; then a scripted call with -TargetRoot
Expected: Double-click picks a folder, restores, and holds the window showing the code; the cmd /c no-arg call RETURNS rather than blocking; the scripted call neither prompts nor holds and returns the SR-040 code.

Parameters: Double-click RECONSTRUCT.command on macOS from an exFAT volume, and after a zip round-trip onto APFS
Expected: From exFAT it launches and restores. From APFS-after-zip Finder refuses until chmod +x, which is the documented limit of the claim; bash reconstruct.sh --pick-target works in both cases.

Parameters: A completed backup and its dated snapshot
Expected: Both contain all seven kit artifacts, including RECONSTRUCT.cmd and RECONSTRUCT.command, and the kit is staged BEFORE the publish rename.

Parameters: A backup root carrying a leftover RECONSTRUCT.bat from a pre-rev-10 store
Expected: It is treated as root-level infrastructure: no orphan or not-in-DB WARN, and no manifest row.

Parameters: The KitRevision markers in Reconstruct.ps1 and bash/reconstruct.sh
Expected: Both read 11 and are equal (AMENDED 2026-09-01, WP17 Part A: 10 -> 11 for the kit-bundled Common.psm1 extension-list and comment edit, Owner ruling Q1). The pin lives in tests/Unit/RestoreLaunchers.Tests.ps1:84. WP16's TC-216 pins the same fact; whichever of WP16/WP17 lands SECOND takes 12 and MERGES the two cases in its own commit. Nothing pinned them before, which is how they drifted to 8 and 6 while the project documented 9.

Parameters: A pool object marked read-only, restored by both restorers
Expected: The restored file is WRITABLE, its bytes verify, and it carries its own mtime. A restored tree is ordinary writable files even when the store is protected.

Parameters: gen_cases: root=set{volume,ordinary} x location=set{root,nested} x folder x side. Volume roots are made with `subst` so they are GENUINE roots, not folders standing in for one.
Expected: True only when the root is a volume root AND the folder is at its root level. At an ORDINARY root - a user's project folder containing '$RECYCLE.BIN' - False, because excluding it is silent data loss. Nested is False everywhere (B6).

Parameters: gen_cases pairwise case 1/4: location=nested, folder=$RECYCLE.BIN, side=backup (plus the root-level $RECYCLE.BIN that must NOT be enumerated)
Expected: Ordinary files are enumerated; nothing under the root-level $RECYCLE.BIN is (deleted files are not backup material); the nested folder's files ARE.

Parameters: gen_cases pairwise case 4/4: location=root, folder=System Volume Information, side=backup
Expected: No enumeration-error record names it, so the set is not marked failed; its contents are not enumerated; the rest of the tree is. Previously a SourcePath at a volume root failed EVERY run.

Parameters: The restorer's pool scan over a store whose root carries a volume-root pseudo-folder
Expected: Both the candidate list and the enumeration errors are filtered, so no StorageUnreadable / exit 4 is reported against an intact store. Filtering only one half would leave the false verdict in place.

Parameters: gen_cases pairwise case 2/4: userland=BSD, mode=HashAddressed_Compress, origin=snapshot (GNU stat/mktemp/find shimmed off PATH; compressed fixture store restored from a dated snapshot)
Expected: The snapshot restores byte-exact, exit 0. This is the ONLY combination that drives the mktemp fix (every compressed row would otherwise fail and be blamed on 7-Zip) and the find -printf fix (the pool would otherwise lose every sibling snapshot) through a REAL restore rather than as isolated units.

Parameters: gen_cases pairwise cases 2/4 and 3/4: side=restore, both folders at the root plus a nested one. A DENY ACE on the unreadable folder (a merely-named folder is readable and never raises the error), the victim row's DataPath blanked AND its pool object deleted, so the pool scan both RUNS and FAILS.
Expected: Exit 1 with ContentMissing in the log and no StorageUnreadable; the undamaged row still restores byte-exact (SR-029). Without the filter this returns 4 - 'fix this host and retry' - for content that is genuinely gone. NOTE: an INTACT store restores with exit 0 either way, because the locator returns on finding the bytes and only consults host issues when it does not; asserting exit 0 here passes against a broken restorer, which two earlier versions of this case did.

Parameters: A real junction 'outside\link' -> the backup root; -TargetRoot outside\link\restore. Plus a genuinely external target, a prefix-sharing sibling, and a nested target.
Expected: The junction target is recognised as INSIDE the backup and refused; the other three keep their existing outcomes. A lexical comparison judges the junction outside and writes into the backup.

Parameters: A BSD userland shim layer that INCLUDES a `touch` rejecting -d; the same store restored with and without the shims; restored mtimes compared.
Expected: The BSD restore reproduces the same instant as the GNU one, and it is the row's own stamp rather than the moment of restore. Without a `touch` shim the suite silently exercises GNU `touch -d` and never reaches the fallback at all.

Parameters: Invoke-OnStaThread driven from a genuinely MTA host - a `pwsh -MTA` child process, because 7.3+ is STA in-process and the path is otherwise unreachable.
Expected: The scriptblock runs on STA, its value crosses back, and the child EXITS 0. The raw-thread version throws an unhandled PSInvalidOperationException on a background thread and terminates the process (observed exit -532462766), so the exit code is asserted as well as the value. Every other picker test injects a -Picker and never reaches the marshalling at all, which is how the broken version survived.

Parameters: FILEBACKUP_PICKER set to an executable whose PATH CONTAINS SPACES, driving a real --pick-target restore.
Expected: The picker runs and the store restores byte-exact. Unquoted, the variable word-splits and the first fragment is executed instead - '/opt/FileBackup Tools/picker' runs '/opt/FileBackup'.

Parameters: A staging lock taken and heartbeated while a deliberately long blocking operation (a large-file hash) occupies the pipeline; the marker's mtime is sampled from a SEPARATE process across several beat intervals. A second variant injects a callback that throws. A third performs a REAL Remove-Module plus Import-Module -Force cycle in a CHILD pwsh process and beats again afterwards (AMENDED 2026-08-31, WP14 §11 R-10: the previous reload case never reloaded the module).
Expected: The mtime advances on the 60 s cadence throughout the blocking operation, proving the compiled callback and not the pipeline drives the beat; the throwing callback neither terminates the run nor leaves the beat silently stopped (System.Timers.Timer swallows handler exceptions, so a dead beat would otherwise look identical to a healthy one). NEGATIVE CONTROL REQUIRED: with the fix removed -- a PowerShell scriptblock or Register-ObjectEvent handler in place of the Add-Type class, or the handle left unrooted -- this case must be shown to FAIL (the mtime stops advancing). An inline or scriptblock beat passes a naive test and fails in production (WP13-T4 precedent).

Parameters: A run killed from outside leaves Temp holding only RUN.inprogress; the marker's mtime is aged past StaleAfterSeconds and the confirmation-sample delay is compressed by a test seam. A second run is then started on the same set.
Expected: The second run takes the confirmation sample, sees the mtime unchanged, moves Temp to Temp.stale-<utc>-<8 hex>, recreates Temp with its own marker, completes with exit 0, and the aside folder is gone (marker leaf deleted by name, directory deleted non-recursively). The log carries [SR-075/reclaimed]. This is the observed HomeHub defect end to end.

Parameters: Temp holding only a RUN.inprogress whose heartbeat is genuinely running (a live owner process); a second run is started against the same ChangePath. Hashes of the whole tree are taken before and after.
Expected: The second run refuses with [SR-075/owner-live] and a message naming the owning host and pid, the start time and the seconds since the last heartbeat; nothing is moved, nothing is deleted, no change folder is written and every file is hash-identical. This is the stomp case that reclaim-by-age alone could not survive.

Parameters: Temp holding a STALE RUN.inprogress plus one or more data files (including a hidden one); SHA-256 of every file in the change root captured before and after the run.
Expected: Refused with [SR-075/content-refused]; the folder is not moved, nothing is deleted, and every hash matches -- asserted as hashes, not merely as presence. This is invariant I-1: a Temp holding data may hold the only physical copy of snapshot-demanded bytes.

Parameters: Reclaim of a stale marker-only Temp with a test hook that creates data files in the folder AFTER Get-StagingLockState has classified it and BEFORE the Directory.Move -- the frozen-then-resumed-owner window.
Expected: The move-aside still happens (it is the README's own safe action), the step-4 re-enumeration sees content, the aside folder is KEPT with its bytes intact, the deletes are skipped and the README recovery is printed; the run continues. NEGATIVE CONTROL REQUIRED: with the step-4 re-enumeration removed (classification trusted through the move) this case must be shown to FAIL by deleting the injected files.

Parameters: Temp holding PRUNE.inprogress, both fresh and aged well past StaleAfterSeconds, with the backup path started against it; plus a real Remove-BackupSnapshot holding the lock for its duration.
Expected: The backup refuses in every case with [SR-075/prune-held] and moves nothing -- age is irrelevant to a prune marker, which WP14 does not own (a killed prune remains WP15). Prune's own staging-busy refusal and its marker are unchanged, so this is also the SR-046 mutual-exclusion regression (invariant I-3).

Parameters: Two runs started concurrently against one stale marker-only Temp, released together at the classification barrier so both reach the Directory.Move.
Expected: Exactly one proceeds; the loser fails the move (or the subsequent New-Item) and refuses without retrying in a loop. Afterwards exactly one Temp exists and its RUN.inprogress carries the WINNER's RunId, and no aside folder survives holding anything but a marker. A DETERMINISTIC INTERLEAVING is also required (AMENDED 2026-08-31, WP14 §11 R-3): reclaimer B stalled at a test seam between its confirmation sample and its move while reclaimer A completes its whole reclaim, so B's move takes A's freshly recreated LIVE Temp -- B must detect the identity mismatch after the move, move the folder straight BACK and refuse, leaving A's marker intact at the original path and no aside folder behind. NEGATIVE CONTROL REQUIRED: with the atomic move replaced by a delete-then-create, or the step-3 New-Item given -Force, this case must be shown to FAIL (both proceed, or the marker is the loser's). Invariant I-2.

Parameters: An EMPTY Temp with no marker, run twice: once with the directory's own mtime aged past the threshold (a pre-WP14 store, which is literally the hub's state) and once with it freshly created (a live run inside its create-to-marker window).
Expected: Stale directory mtime is reclaimed and the run completes, so the upgrade path from a pre-WP14 store costs nothing; fresh directory mtime is REFUSED, which is the gate that stops a reclaimer stealing a live lock in the microseconds between New-Item and the marker publish.

Parameters: A RUN.inprogress whose mtime is set into the future relative to the reader, at offsets both inside and far beyond the threshold, fed through Read-StagingOwnerRecord and Get-StagingLockState.
Expected: Classified OwnerLive and refused. Clock skew is handled conservatively in the harmless direction: a future mtime can only be a clock disagreement, never proof of death.

Parameters: The G8 real-volume suite on Windows against an actual exFAT-formatted volume: a stale marker-only Temp reclaimed end to end, plus an ambiguous Directory.Move failure injected on the same volume.
Expected: The reclaim completes on exFAT with the aside folder removed and the run at exit 0, and the injected move failure REFUSES with both paths untouched and no writer started -- never a fallback to delete. Half of the plan's Q1 evidence: .NET does not promise rename atomicity, so the supported-provider list is defined from this evidence.

Parameters: Container acceptance inside filebackup:local on the deployment's Linux-over-exFAT bind mount: the same stale-marker reclaim, with the boot id read from /proc and the host and container id recorded in the marker.
Expected: The reclaim completes inside the container and the run reaches exit 0; the record's diagnostic identity fields are populated from the container's own view. This is the deployment the defect was actually found in, and the other half of Q1 -- one Windows run is not evidence for this stack.

Parameters: The existing TC-073 staging-cleanup case and the four catch cleanups re-run unchanged, plus an exception injected at each major phase AFTER staging has gained content.
Expected: TC-073 and the four catch cleanups remain green, and in every injected-exception case the heartbeat is stopped and drained by the Part B finally -- no live timer is left advertising an abandoned lock as owned, and the successor run therefore classifies it OwnerStale rather than OwnerLive. The catch blocks alone cover only the early exits, which is the regression risk this case exists for.

Parameters: Run A paused by a test hook AFTER its New-Item of Temp and BEFORE the marker publish; run B meanwhile classifies the empty directory per TC-192 and reclaims it; run A is then released.
Expected: A's exclusive FileMode.CreateNew publish FAILS because RUN.inprogress now exists (B's), and A aborts immediately, touching nothing -- no move, no delete, no change folder, and NOTHING left in B's Temp, which holds its own RUN.inprogress and nothing else (AMENDED 2026-08-31, WP14 §11 R-4: the old temp-write publish could strand a '.tmp' in a folder A no longer owned, itself a permanent wedge) -- logging [SR-075/lock-lost]. NEGATIVE CONTROL REQUIRED: with the publish made non-exclusive (a create-or-truncate write) this case must be shown to FAIL, with A silently continuing to write into B's staging folder. The window is microseconds wide; correctness must not depend on that.

Parameters: A reclaim whose test hook drops a data file into the ASIDE folder between the step-4 re-enumeration and the delete -- the last window in the protocol.
Expected: The exact-leaf marker delete may succeed, but the non-recursive Directory.Delete then FAILS because the directory is not empty; the aside folder is kept with the injected bytes intact, the failure is logged loudly with the README recovery, and the run continues. NEGATIVE CONTROL REQUIRED: with a recursive delete restored in place of the non-recursive one, this case must be shown to FAIL by destroying the injected file. This race is the entire reason -Recurse is banned from the reclaim path.

Parameters: Read-StagingOwnerRecord and Get-StagingLockState against a truncated marker, a marker of unknown SchemaVersion, a marker whose StaleAfterSeconds is BELOW 1800 s, and a marker held open with a deny-read lock or an ACL that blocks reading -- each at both stale and fresh mtimes.
Expected: Truncated and unknown-schema markers return ParseInvalid with LastWriteUtc and AgeSeconds populated and fall back to mtime alone with the 1800 s reader floor applied (a below-floor StaleAfterSeconds cannot shorten it), reclaiming when stale and refusing when fresh; ParseInvalid is never an error, because a torn record is precisely a writer that died mid-publish and refusing it would recreate the permanent wedge for the commonest crash. The unreadable marker returns Unreadable and REFUSES: absence of evidence is not evidence of death.

Parameters: Get-StagingLockState fed enumerations containing hidden, system and dot-named entries; an enumeration that raises an I/O or access error; and a Temp that is a symlink/junction to another tree.
Expected: Hidden, system and dot-named entries all classify HoldsContent -- forced enumeration means they are content like any other. An enumeration, stat or access failure classifies Indeterminate and refuses: an I/O error is never evidence of emptiness. A reparse-point Temp is refused outright, because moving or deleting through one acts on a tree the guard never classified.

Parameters: A heartbeat callback deliberately held in flight (a test seam blocking inside the touch) across a Stop-StagingHeartbeat call, while a successor acquires Temp and publishes a marker with a DIFFERENT RunId; the held callback is then released.
Expected: Stop blocks until the in-flight callback drains, and the released callback finds a RunId that is not its own and does not touch: the successor's marker mtime is NOT freshened, so the successor's own staleness is judged on its own beat. Stop is also idempotent when called twice. NEGATIVE CONTROL REQUIRED: with either layer removed -- the drain or the RunId identity guard -- this case must be shown to FAIL by freshening the successor's marker.

Parameters: A full changed-run finalize through Complete-ChangeFolder, plus the no-op and first-run paths, each starting from a staging lock that carried a RUN.inprogress; the produced Snapshot_* is then pruned.
Expected: No RUN.inprogress exists anywhere inside the produced Snapshot_* on any of the three paths -- the marker is stopped, drained and deleted as a leaf immediately before finalize -- and that snapshot prunes WITHOUT an unreferenced-data refusal. Left in place, the marker would be renamed wholesale into every snapshot and then refused by SR-046's rail as a file its manifest does not name.

Parameters: The writer's clock set BEHIND the reader's by more than StaleAfterSeconds (the marker therefore reads as long stale on first sample) while the owner is genuinely alive and beating; the reader then takes its confirmation sample.
Expected: The confirmation sample sees the mtime MOVE, so the owner is judged live and the run is refused with [SR-075/owner-live] -- no clock configuration can cause a live owner to be stomped, because the second sample is clock-free. NEGATIVE CONTROL REQUIRED: with the confirmation sample removed (age alone deciding), this case must be shown to FAIL by reclaiming a live owner's lock. This is the skew direction the first draft had backwards.

Parameters: A test hook that swaps Temp's RUN.inprogress for one carrying a different RunId, applied at each of the FIVE fence points in turn: before the step-7 staging manifest write, before Move-RemovedFilesToStaging, before Save-SupersededData, before the backup-root MANIFEST.csv publish and before Complete-ChangeFolder (AMENDED 2026-08-31, WP14 §11 R-2/R-10).
Expected: At every fence the run aborts BEFORE that phase mutates the pool or publishes state, cleans up NOTHING (the folder is no longer its own to delete), and logs [SR-075/lock-lost]. Per fence: no stored data byte ceases to exist anywhere in the store, the snapshot set and FileBackupState.json are unchanged, and MANIFEST.csv and its DIRECTORIES.csv sidecar are unchanged at every fence that precedes the backup-root publish. At the finalize fence -- the only one that FOLLOWS that publish, the run having still owned the lock one step earlier -- the manifest is this run's own canonical step-12 output and nothing was finalized over it. NEGATIVE CONTROL REQUIRED: with the fence check removed at each point IN TURN, this case must be shown to FAIL -- the run proceeds past that boundary, finalizes a snapshot, deletes the successor's owner record and publishes state.

Parameters: Every extension WP17 Part A appends to $script:NonCompressibleExtensions - .z7 .esd .mpg .mpeg .m2ts .m4v .wmv .flv .heic .heif .opus .m4a - in lower, upper and mixed case; plus the deliberate NON-additions .iso .mca .bin .dng .pdf.
Expected: Test-ShouldCompress returns $false for every added extension and is case-insensitive; .iso still returns $true, pinning the deliberate non-addition (a filesystem CONTAINER is not already-compressed content, and adding it would be the false-'already compressed' error the defect review names). The list stays defined in exactly ONE place in Common and Engine holds no NonCompressibleExtensions reference (with TC-096). .z7 is the finding itself: 649 objects, 880 GB, 43% of the production library.

Parameters: Measure-SampleCompressibility called directly via InModuleScope over synthetic corpora BUILT IN THE TEST: pure random bytes; repeated text; a random file with a 64 KiB text head; a file one third text; a 500 KiB file; a 4 KiB file; an empty file; a vanished path; and a path held open with FileShare.None. Constants read through InModuleScope ($script:CompressProbeThreshold 0.10, $script:CompressProbeMinBytes 262144).
Expected: Aggregate CompressedBytes/SampledBytes is approximately 1.0 for random, far below 1 for text, approximately 0.93 for the mixed-head file (so the aggregate rule keeps it RAW where an any-sample rule would have compressed it - the defect review's own failure mode) and approximately 0.7 for the mixed-third file (so it COMPRESSES). The 500 KiB file is below Samples x SampleBytes and is therefore read exactly ONCE as a single whole-file sample, not as three overlapping windows. The vanished path and the FileShare.None-locked path each return $null rather than throwing. Random bytes must NOT measure below 0.98, which is the assertion that pins the compressed count being taken AFTER Dispose() - a count read before the encoder is closed reads short and would call random bytes compressible. Offsets are 0, floor((len - SampleBytes)/2) and len - SampleBytes, and the open uses FileShare.Read.

Parameters: A full backup run per arm, mode always and then mode off, above the 256 KiB floor: a .docx whose bytes are random, a .jpg whose bytes are text, and a .txt. The Owner's Q7 ruling under test.
Expected: Under always: the .docx over random bytes is stored RAW with Compressed=No; the .jpg over text bytes is stored as .7z with Compressed=Yes; the .txt is stored .7z. Under off the SAME three files take today's list answer - .7z, raw, .7z - so the pre-WP17 behaviour and SN-003's illustration are still reproducible on demand. No Reason value named after a file format exists anywhere in the decision, and Resolve-CompressionDecision takes no name-based override input: this case is the PIN on Owner ruling Q7 (2026-09-01), that SN-003's acceptance extensions are examples of the need and the bytes, not the names, decide. Filename extension and the Compressed column agree in all six arms.

Parameters: Mode always, every file above the 256 KiB floor: an unlisted extension and a no-extension file over each of random, text, mixed-head and mixed-third content; plus a LISTED .zip over text and the same .zip over random.
Expected: Random stores raw, text stores .7z, mixed-head (aggregate ~0.93) stores RAW, mixed-third (aggregate ~0.7) stores .7z; the listed .zip over text stores .7z and over random stores raw - the defining property of the default mode, that the list is not consulted above the floor. In every arm the stored filename's extension and the row's Compressed column agree (SR-004's agreement sentence, I-1). NEGATIVE CONTROL REQUIRED: with the probe BYPASSED so the decision falls back to the extension list, this case must be shown to FAIL - the random arms compress.

Parameters: Invoke-BackupFileGroup called DIRECTLY in-process (the suites drive backups through FileBackup.ps1, which re-imports both modules with -Force at FileBackup.ps1:236 and thereby discards any Mock -ModuleName injected earlier; Mock -ModuleName FileBackup.Engine on a direct call has precedent at Coverage.Tests.ps1:1862), with Measure-SampleCompressibility mocked behind a call counter. Arms: a prior-backup dedup hit; an in-run twin; a group whose FIRST member's copy fails and whose second succeeds; a locked owner with a readable twin.
Expected: The dedup hit makes ZERO probe calls and the in-run twin makes zero ADDITIONAL calls - both return before the write branch, which is what keeps SR-061 true (no already-stored object's form is re-decided). The failed-then-twin group makes EXACTLY 1 call and emits at most 1 WARN. The locked-owner group samples the readable TWIN and its decision is NOT ProbeUnavailable. NEGATIVE CONTROL REQUIRED: with the group-scope memo removed, this case must be shown to FAIL - the failed-then-twin arm counts 2 calls (the write branch sits inside foreach ($entry in $Group) and a failed member continues with the written-object memo still null, so a naive lazy expression re-probes per failing member).

Parameters: CompressProbe across both configuration formats, driven from the ONE shared fixture corpus tests/Common/ConfigFixtures.ps1. Accepted: off, excluded-extensions, always, and the key ABSENT. Rejected: "Always" (mixed case), "maybe", null and a number. Plus TC-225's inputs replayed under off and under excluded-extensions, and an unchanged v2 config.
Expected: off reproduces the pre-WP17 decision for TC-225's inputs exactly; excluded-extensions stores the listed .zip-over-text RAW (the list still exempts) while still probing the unlisted arms; an absent key resolves to always and the object Resolve-BackupSetDefaults returns CARRIES the value (without the key in its fixed field list a validated key is silently dropped). Each of "Always", "maybe", null and a number aborts with exit 2 NAMING the key, creating nothing, in JSON AND in CLIXML - the CLIXML arms are what prove the value check lives in Test-BackupConfigurationShape beside the BrowseView block (-cnotin) and not only in the JSON-only closed key set. The published container/FileBackup.schema.json enum equals the validator's vocabulary (TC-077 parity). An unchanged v2 configuration still loads with ConfigVersion 2, and TC-074, TC-075 and TC-077 stay green on the shared corpus.

Parameters: Invoke-BackupFileGroup called DIRECTLY, with a REAL FileShare.None handle held on EVERY member of the group so no candidate can be opened. Mode always, file above the floor.
Expected: The decision is ProbeUnavailable and its Compress value is THE LIST'S ANSWER - today's behaviour, not a default of 'compress' - with exactly one WARN emitted, and the run exits 0. Fail-toward-today, never fail-the-run: a lock costs a decision, never a file (I-6). No probe error propagates, and the destination is never opened.

Parameters: -Action Verify over a probe-MIXED store (objects in both storage forms, some raw-stored with archive-magic bytes under their own .z7 name) using TC-093's harness, non-Deep and then -Deep, with Get-FileXxHash mocked behind a call counter. Then a full restore of the same store by Reconstruct.ps1 and by bash/reconstruct.sh.
Expected: The audit reports CLEAN over the probe-mixed store - both forms are still just forms. A raw-stored .z7 (Compressed=No over 7-Zip magic) whose DataPath extension equals the row's RelativePath extension and whose on-disk length equals the row's Length is EXEMPTED WITHOUT A HASH: the mocked Get-FileXxHash counter is 0 on the non-Deep scan and greater than 0 under -Deep, where the confirming hash is retained. This is what stops Part A turning a 'rare' shape into 880 GB of re-hashing on every Verify pass. Reconstruct.ps1 and reconstruct.sh each reproduce every object BYTE-EXACT from the mixed store.

Parameters: TC-225's arms re-run INSIDE the filebackup:local container image on the Linux stack, mode always, with the set summary captured.
Expected: Every TC-225 assertion holds inside the image - Linux is where the defect was measured, so the fix is proven there. The summary REPORTS the 'Probe reads: <bytes>' counter and the wall time the probe cost, so the first-run cost claim is MEASURED rather than asserted; the figures are recorded, and no pass budget is set until there is production data to set one from (no PB row is invented here).
